# PDF

One or more PDF files the customer provides locally: manuals, guides, exported specs. There is no navigation data or URL space, so structure comes from the PDF outline and headings.

## Detect

- The customer points you at `.pdf` files, or the current directory holds them.
- Check each file before choosing a method:
  - `pdfinfo file.pdf` for page count and producer.
  - `pdffonts file.pdf`: no fonts listed means scanned pages (images only).
  - `pdftotext -f 1 -l 3 file.pdf - | head`: empty or garbled output also means scanned or broken text encoding.

## Get the source

### From the repo

Not applicable; the customer provides the PDF files.

### From an export

The PDFs are the source. Copy them unchanged into `mirror/` and work from the copies.

Extract in this order of preference:

1. **Native PDF reading**, if your tool reads PDFs directly with layout. Still render pages to images for table and figure checks (below).
2. **PyMuPDF** (`pip install pymupdf`, imported as `fitz`) for structure. `page.get_text("dict")` returns blocks, lines and spans with font name, size and flags (bold, italic, monospace); use these to rebuild headings and code. `page.find_tables()` locates tables.
3. **Poppler** for plain text: `pdftotext -layout -f N -l M file.pdf out.txt` keeps columns and table alignment; `pdftohtml -xml file.pdf out` gives positioned text with font specs when PyMuPDF is unavailable.

Render each page to an image for checking: `pdftoppm -png -r 110 -f N -l N file.pdf mirror/pages/p` or PyMuPDF `page.get_pixmap(dpi=110).save(...)`.

**Scanned PDFs.** Run OCR into a new file and extract from that: `ocrmypdf --skip-text file.pdf mirror/file.ocr.pdf` (add `-l <lang>` for non-English). Mark every page converted from OCR in the manifest `notes` as `ocr` and list them in the report; OCR text needs a human proofread.

Encrypted PDFs that refuse extraction: ask the customer for an unlocked copy. Never try to bypass the protection.

### From the live site

Not applicable.

## Config → docs.json

| PDF                                               | docs.json                                                              |
| ------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Document title (title page or metadata)           | `name`, if the customer has no product name to use                     |
| Logo on the title page                            | `logo`, only if the customer confirms it                               |
| Several PDFs                                      | one group per PDF, or `navigation.tabs` if they are separate manuals   |
| Title page, copyright page, revision history      | a page only if it has content readers need; else exclude with a reason |
| Printed table of contents, index, list of figures | drop; navigation and search replace them                               |
| Running headers, footers, page numbers            | drop                                                                   |

## Navigation

The outline (bookmarks) is the navigation data:

```python
import fitz
for level, title, page in fitz.open("mirror/file.pdf").get_toc():
    print(level, page, title)
```

Without PyMuPDF, `qpdf --json --json-key=outlines file.pdf` exposes the same outline.

- Level 1 entries become groups (or pages, if they have no children); deeper levels become nested groups and pages. Keep labels verbatim.
- Choose a page split depth (usually level 2) and apply it uniformly. Each page covers from its outline entry's page to the page before the next entry at the same or higher level.
- An outline entry can start mid-page; split at its heading, not at the page break.
- No outline: derive the tree from heading font sizes (largest size = level 1) and confirm the result with the customer before converting. The printed table of contents is a fallback source of titles and page numbers.

## Content conversion

Never paraphrase, summarize or reword. Every word on a page comes from the PDF.

- **Page furniture.** Strip running headers, footers and page numbers: lines that repeat at the same position on most pages. Detect them by position and repetition, not by guessing text.
- **Line and page breaks.** Rejoin lines inside paragraphs; rejoin paragraphs split across a page break. Remove end-of-line hyphenation only where the joined word is a real word (`config-\nuration` → `configuration`); keep hyphens in compounds (`command-\nline` stays `command-line` when that is how the document spells it elsewhere).
- **Headings.** Map font size and weight to heading levels per document. The page's own title becomes frontmatter `title` (`mint migrate --topic conversion`, Frontmatter).
- **Lists.** Rebuild bullets (`•`, `–`, `▪`) and numbered items, including nesting by indent. Join wrapped list lines.
- **Tables.** The main hazard. Extracted text loses cell boundaries, merges multi-line cells and splits tables across pages. Rebuild each table, then compare it cell by cell against the rendered page image. Merge continued tables (repeated header row on the next page). Use an HTML table only where cells span rows or columns.
- **Code.** Monospace spans become fenced blocks. Keep indentation and line breaks exactly; do not rejoin code lines. Add a language only when the document states it or it is unambiguous.
- **Callouts.** Boxed "Note", "Caution", "Warning" or "Tip" paragraphs map to the matching callout component, only where the label is printed.
- **Ligatures and characters.** Normalize ligatures (`ﬁ`, `ﬂ`), curly quotes in code, and non-breaking spaces. Unknown glyphs (`�`) mean an encoding problem: re-extract that page with another tool or OCR it.
- **Cross-references.** "See section 4.2" and "on page 37" become links to the migrated page that holds that content; keep the original wording.
- **Footnotes.** Move each footnote to the end of its page's section, keeping its number.

## Assets

- Extract embedded images per page: `pdfimages -png -f N -l N file.pdf images/<page-path>/fig` (use `-all` to keep original formats).
- Vector diagrams are not images: crop the region from a high-DPI render (`page.get_pixmap(clip=rect, dpi=200)`).
- Alt text comes from the figure caption, verbatim. No caption means alt text from the nearest heading plus "figure"; record it in the report. Put the caption in `<Frame caption>`.
- Drop decorative images (logos repeated on every page, rules, backgrounds).

## URLs and redirects

PDFs have no URLs, so there are no redirects. Instead, record the page range of every migrated page in the manifest, using `source_url` for the file and page range: `"source_url": "manual.pdf#pages=12-18"`. Every page of every PDF maps to exactly one migrated page or is `excluded` with a reason (title page, printed table of contents, blank page). If the customer links to the PDF from elsewhere, tell them which new page replaces each section.

## Known gaps

- OCR accuracy on scanned pages.
- Complex tables (merged cells, rotated headers, multi-page tables) need manual review against the page image.
- Vector diagrams become raster crops.
- Form fields, annotations, embedded attachments and hyperlinks inside the PDF may not survive extraction; check with `pdfinfo` and PyMuPDF `page.get_links()` and report what is lost.
- Equations: rebuild as LaTeX only where the text is extractable; otherwise use an image of the equation and report it.
